title: The Hard Cipher
premise: Petra Crane, a deniable fixer for an embassy that exists on no map, is repaid for a favor she has no memory of performing when a stranger named Elias Voss delivers evidence of a buried massacre implicating all three governments she serves. Hunted by an assassin called the Archivist who erases witnesses along with records, Petra and Elias must smuggle the truth through forged channels, betrayed allies, and her own fractured memory — because the missing favor turns out to be something Petra did and was made to forget. In the end, she chooses exposure over survival, broadcasting the cipher publicly at the cost of her old life, and finds a new family among the people the truth saves.
about_author: Marguerite Hartwell is a former diplomatic translator who spent a decade in cities that appear on maps but not in official histories. She writes thrillers about the people governments prefer to forget, from a farmhouse whose location she declines to confirm.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A quiet Tuesday in Vienna shatters when Elias Voss appears at her safehouse café, thanking her for a rescue she cannot remember and handing her a sealed drive as 'interest owed.' The beat: unease — her own memory has a hole in it, and someone else knows its shape.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He explains the drive contains the Halvard File: proof of a joint operation that slaughtered a village and rewrote every record. Before he can finish, the café's cameras die in sequence. The beat: dread arriving on schedule.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV, unnamed. We meet the killer mid-cleanup, burning a witness's identity out of existence with bureaucratic tenderness. He receives Petra's photograph. The beat: cold professionalism hiding a personal obsession with completeness.

chapters.title: Deniable Assets
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She runs the drive through embassy back-channels and watches three governments simultaneously deny the file exists while quietly mobilizing to retrieve it. Her handler orders her to surrender Elias. The beat: loyalty curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Hiding in a tram depot, he and Petra count their options like coins: two days of safety, one border, no allies. He reveals he found her name stitched inside the file itself. The beat: reluctant partnership becoming trust.

chapters.title: What Petra Forgot
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, fragmented flashbacks. Chasing the memory gap, she finds a clinic receipt dated the night of the Halvard operation. She didn't just witness it — she pulled Elias out of it, then chose to forget. The beat: vertigo of self-betrayal.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Bullet
chapters.summary: Handler's POV. A tri-national coordination call decides the file must be destroyed and its carriers 'retired.' Petra listens on a hidden line, hearing her own death scheduled politely. The beat: betrayal made administrative.

chapters.title: The Border at Bratislava
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A crossing goes wrong; Elias takes a graze wound covering Petra's escape, and she carries him rather than abandon him. The beat: found family forming under fire — she protects him before she decides to.

chapters.title: Cipher Work
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Decoding the file's encryption, they discover it needs a key held by Nadia Okafor, a disgraced archivist living ghost-quiet in Trieste — the last person who processed the original records. The beat: hope with a price tag.

chapters.title: Nadia
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. The ex-archivist agrees to help but warns them the Archivist was once her colleague — a man who believes deleting people is mercy. The beat: fear tempered by unexpected kinship among the erased.

chapters.title: Trieste Interlude
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. One night of borrowed normalcy: cooking, laughter, Petra almost smiling. Then Nadia's window sensors trip. The beat: warmth sharpened by its imminent loss.

chapters.title: The Archive Burns
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. The Archivist attacks; Nadia dies buying them minutes, pressing the key into Petra's hand. The beat: grief converted directly into resolve.

chapters.title: Running the Ledger
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. With the key, the full file opens — including footage of Petra herself, masked, carrying wounded Elias out. Her forgotten heroism becomes the file's most dangerous corroboration. The beat: memory reclaimed as weapon.

chapters.title: The Handler's Offer
chapters.summary: Handler's POV then Petra's. Her handler offers reinstatement, protection, a clean slate — if she surrenders the file and lets Elias be archived. The beat: temptation framed as kindness; she refuses.

chapters.title: Ghost Network
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. They assemble the people the system discarded — a forger, a retired signals officer, a journalist in exile — a found family of loose ends. The beat: belonging built from damage.

chapters.title: The Journalist's Gamble
chapters.summary: Journalist POV. Publishing requires verification and a live source; both make targets. They plan a simultaneous triple broadcast across three jurisdictions so no single government can bury it. The beat: audacity as strategy.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Archivist's POV. He infiltrates the network through the forger, who vanishes mid-task. Petra realizes too late the broadcast site is compromised. The beat: the trap closing with quiet clicks.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Relay
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Cornered at the transmission relay, she faces the Archivist and offers him what he truly wants — not death, but acknowledgment that some things should stay remembered. He hesitates. The beat: humanity flickering inside the machine.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Braided POVs. Under fire, Elias holds the uplink while Petra transmits the Halvard File to three continents. The Archivist, given the choice to stop her, instead walks away and deletes his own contract. The beat: climax — truth escaping its cage.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Official Version
chapters.summary: Handler's POV. Governments scramble, resignations cascade, and Petra is officially declared dead — the cleanest ending they can buy. The beat: bitter irony dressed as victory.

chapters.title: Unofficial Version
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Alive under a new name, she meets Elias, the signals officer, and the journalist at a coastal table with no cameras. The family holds. The beat: peace earned, not granted.

chapters.title: The Hard Cipher
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Petra's POV, letter-like narration. She explains the title: the hardest code to break is the one you keep against yourself, and justice outside the law still requires someone willing to remember. The beat: resolution — memory chosen freely at last.
